41271-history-of-the-johnstown-flood-inc.creator: Unknown
41271-history-of-the-johnstown-flood-inc.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The summer of 1889 will ever be memorable for its appalling disasters by flood and flame. In that period fell the heaviest blow of the nineteenth century--a blow scarcely paralleled in the histories of civilized lands. Central Pennsylvania, a centre of industry, thrift and comfort, was desolated by floods unprecedented in the records of the great waters.

arxiv-2105-10563.title: Puck localization and multi-task event recognition in broadcast hockey videos
arxiv-2105-10563.creator: Kanav Vats Mehrnaz Fani David A. Clausi John Zelek University of Waterloo Waterloo, Ontario, Canada {k2vats, mfani, dclausi,jzelek}@uwaterloo.ca
arxiv-2105-10563.description: Abstract Puck localization is an important problem in ice hockey video analytics useful for analyzing the game, determining play location, and assessing puck possession. The problem is challenging due to the small size of the puck, excessive motion blur due to high puck velocity and occlusions due to players and boards.

arxiv-2308-07502.title: SpecTracle: Wearable Facial Motion Tracking from Unobtrusive Peripheral Cameras
arxiv-2308-07502.creator: Yinan Xuan, Varun Viswanath, Sunny Chu, Owen Bartolf, Jessica Echterhoff, Edward Wang *
arxiv-2308-07502.description: Abstract Facial motion tracking in head-mounted displays (HMD) has the potential to enable immersive ”face-to-face” interaction in a virtual environment. However, current works on facial tracking are not suitable for unobtrusive augmented reality (AR) glasses or do not have the ability to track arbitrary facial movements.

arxiv-2406-08098.title: Scalable Defect Detection via Traversal on Code Graph
arxiv-2406-08098.creator: Zhengyao Liu, Xitong Zhong, Xingjing Deng, Shuo Hong, Xiang Gao, Hailong Sun
arxiv-2406-08098.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhengyao Liu, Xitong Zhong, Xingjing Deng, Shuo Hong, Xiang Gao, Hailong Sun. Detecting defects and vulnerabilities in the early stage has long been a challenge in software engineering. Static analysis, a technique that inspects code without execution, has emerged as a key strategy to address this challenge. Among recent advancements, the use of graph-based representations, particularly Code Property Graph (CPG), has gained traction due to its comprehensive depiction of code structure and semantics.

arxiv-2407-09632.title: Granger Causality in Extremes
arxiv-2407-09632.creator: Juraj Bodik, Olivier C. Pasche
arxiv-2407-09632.description: Abstract Causal discovery in time series becomes especially important during extreme, highly volatile periods, yet state-of-the-art methods focus on causality within the body of the distribution and often overlook mechanisms that manifest only in extreme events. We propose a framework for Granger causality in extremes that infers causal links primarily from extreme events, using the causal tail coefficient.

arxiv-2501-02946.title: Geometric Brownian Information Engine: Time evolution of extractable work, power, and efficiency
arxiv-2501-02946.creator: Syed Yunus Ali, Rafna Rafeek, Debasish Mondal
arxiv-2501-02946.description: Abstract We explore the effects of finite cycle period time ( τ \tau ) on the extractable work, power, and efficiency of the Geometric Brownian Information Engine (GBIE). The GBIE consists of overdamped Brownian particles confined within a monolobal geometry.

arxiv-2503-05448.title: Joint graphical model estimation using Stein-type shrinkage for fast large scale network inference in scRNAseq data
arxiv-2503-05448.creator: Duong H.T. Vo, Nelofer Syed, Thomas Thorne
arxiv-2503-05448.description: Abstract Graphical modeling is a widely used tool for analyzing conditional dependencies between variables and traditional methods may struggle to capture shared and distinct structures in multi-group or multi-condition settings. Joint graphical modeling (JGM) extends this framework by simultaneously estimating network structures across multiple related datasets, allowing for a deeper understanding of commonalities and differences.

arxiv-2508-10261.title: Attosecond Transient Absorption Study of Coherent Hole Oscillation in Ar +
arxiv-2508-10261.creator: Nisnat Chakraborty 1 , Miguel Alarcón 1 , Michael P. McDonnell 1 , Karl Hauser 1 , Islam Shalaby 1 , Dipayan Biswas 1 , James K. Wood 2 , Nikolay V. Golubev 1 , Arvinder Sandhu 1,2,3
arxiv-2508-10261.description: Abstract We report on the observation, characterization, and control of the electron dynamics in ionized argon atoms. We utilized an intense mid-infrared (MIR) pulse to create a coherent superposition of the spin-orbit split ground state of the ion. A weak extreme ultraviolet (XUV) pulse then probes the hole oscillation through time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy.

europmc-pmc7400514.title: A deep learning model to predict RNA-Seq expression of tumours from whole slide images.
europmc-pmc7400514.creator: Schmauch B, Romagnoni A, Pronier E, Saillard C, Maillé P, Calderaro J, Kamoun A, Sefta M, Toldo S, Zaslavskiy M, Clozel T, Moarii M, Courtiol P, Wainrib G.
europmc-pmc7400514.description: Deep learning methods for digital pathology analysis are an effective way to address multiple clinical questions, from diagnosis to prediction of treatment outcomes. These methods have also been used to predict gene mutations from pathology images, but no comprehensive...

pmc-10548253.title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of Argemone mexicana-inspired antimicrobials
pmc-10548253.creator: Jessica Villegas, Bryce C Ball, Katelyn M Shouse, Caleb W VanArragon, Ashley N Wasserman, Hannah E Bhakta, Allen G Oliver, Danielle A Orozco-Nunnelly, Jeffrey M Pruet, David Spring
pmc-10548253.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Due to the lack of new antimicrobial drug discovery in recent years and an ever-growing prevalence of multidrug-resistant “superbugs”, there is a pressing need to explore alternative ways to combat pathogenic bacterial and fungal infections. Building upon our previous work in the field of medicinal phytochemistry, the present study is focused on designing, synthesizing, and testing the altered bioactivity of new variants of two original bioactive molecules found in the Argemone mexicana plant.

pmc-10605448.title: Accelerated Aging and the Life Course of Individuals Born Preterm
pmc-10605448.creator: Audrey Bousquet, Keia Sanderson, T Michael O’Shea, Rebecca C Fry, Susan R Hintz, Jonathan Samuel Litt, Srinivas Bolisetty
pmc-10605448.description: Individuals born preterm have shorter lifespans and elevated rates of chronic illness that contribute to mortality risk when compared to individuals born at term. Emerging evidence suggests that individuals born preterm or of low birthweight also exhibit physiologic and cellular biomarkers of accelerated aging.

pmc-10674219.title: First Report of Plasmid-Mediated Macrolide-Clindamycin-Tetracycline Resistance in a High Virulent Isolate of Cutibacterium acnes ST115
pmc-10674219.creator: Md Shohel Rana, Jungmin Kim, Shukho Kim, Longzhu Cui
pmc-10674219.description: Cutibacterium acnes, a prevalent skin commensal, has emerged as a significant global challenge due to its widespread antibiotic resistance. To investigate the antibiotic resistance mechanisms and clinical characterization of C. acnes in Korea, we collected 22 clinical isolates from diverse patient specimens obtained from the National Culture Collection for Pathogens across Korea.

pmc-11354167.title: Creating and Reliving the Moment: Using Musical Improvisation and Care Aesthetics as a Lens of Connection and Self-Expression for Younger People Living with Dementia
pmc-11354167.creator: Robyn Dowlen, Dougal Henry James McPherson, Caroline Swarbrick, Lizzie Hoskin, James Thompson, John Keady, Paul M Camic, Mary Pat Sullivan
pmc-11354167.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Musical improvisation is a generative process of spontaneously creating music ‘in the moment’. For people with young onset dementia, musical improvisation provides an extended opportunity for creative self-expression and connection to one’s own body and life story. Using visual research methods, including video elicitation interviews, this paper explores the ‘in the moment’ musical experiences of five people living with young onset dementia who took part in a 15-week improvised music-making programme (Music in Mind).

pmc-11355115.title: DiADEM—Dance against Dementia—Effect of a Six-Month Dance Intervention on Physical Fitness in Older Adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Randomized, Controlled Trial
pmc-11355115.creator: Ulrich Thiel, Marvin Stiebler, Berit K Labott, Johanna Bappert, Corinna Langhans, Nicole Halfpaap, Bernhard Grässler, Fabian Herold, Stefanie Schreiber, Rüdiger Braun-Dullaeus, Patrick Müller, Notger Müller, Anita Hökelmann, Rajendra D Badgaiyan
pmc-11355115.description: Background: Preserving health and physical fitness is critical to ensure independent living across the lifespan. Lower levels of physical fitness are associated with age-related cognitive decline and a higher prevalence of mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Thus, this study investigates the influence of a six-month dance intervention on selected measures of physical fitness in older adults with MCI.

pmc-11384452.title: Surgical strategy and long-term outcomes of dissected carotid artery with false lumen thrombus in acute type A aortic dissection
pmc-11384452.creator: Hongyuan Lin, Hongyan Zhou, Xiaoning Huo, Hongwei Guo, Yi Chang
pmc-11384452.description: BackgroundOptimal management of involved common carotid artery (CCA) with false-lumen thrombus remains unclear in aortic dissection patients. We aim to investigate outcomes and compare different surgical strategies.MethodsThis is a retrospective cohort study and the institutional database of acute type A aortic dissection was reviewed.

pmc-11428811.title: Genomic Analysis of Enterobacter Species Isolated from Patients in United States Hospitals
pmc-11428811.creator: Fred C Tenover, Isabella A Tickler, Kirsty Sands
pmc-11428811.description: We analyzed the whole genome sequences (WGS) and antibiograms of 35 Enterobacter isolates, including E. hormaechei and E. asburiae, and the recently described E. bugandensis, E. kobei, E. ludwigii, and E. roggenkampii species. Isolates were obtained from human blood and urinary tract infections in patients in the United States.

pmc-12397305.title: Self-relevant facial threat attracts peripheral attention
pmc-12397305.creator: David Terburg, Sjoerd Stuit
pmc-12397305.description: Threat-relevance theory suggests that gaze direction determines the self-relevance of facial threats. Indeed, angry eye-contact is a more relevant threat compared to its counterpart with averted gaze. Similarly, fearful eye-contact is not a threat to the observer, but averted fearful gaze can signal a relevant threat nearby.

pmc-12406801.title: The time to care is now: a multidisciplinary call to action for addressing paediatric burn injuries globally
pmc-12406801.creator: Kajsa Vlasic, Theresia Mwakyembe, Irma Fleming, Giavonni Lewis, Sudha Jayaraman, Catherine A Staton, Melissa H Watt, Blandina T Mmbaga, Elizabeth M Keating
pmc-12406801.description: y is caused by an act of war or a cooking incident at home, the consequences are equally devastating for children and their families. Addressing the multiple challenges of paediatric burn injuries requires multidisciplinary coordination to ensure timely access to evidence-based care and comprehensive support for physical recovery, emotional healing and reintegration into daily life.

pmc-12470440.title: Seeding of Dermal Substitutes with Glucose-Pretreated Nanofat Accelerates In Vivo Vascularization and Tissue Integration
pmc-12470440.creator: Valeria Pruzzo, Francesca Bonomi, Ettore Limido, Andrea Weinzierl, Yves Harder, Matthias W Laschke, Chi Lee
pmc-12470440.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The exposure of endothelial cells to high glucose concentrations promotes angiogenesis. The present study investigated whether this pro-angiogenic effect of glucose is suitable to improve the capability of nanofat to vascularize implanted dermal substitutes. Nanofat was processed from white adipose tissue originating from green fluorescent protein (GFP)+ C57BL/6J donor mice and incubated for 1 h in Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution with or without (control) a high level of glucose (30 mM).

pmc-12546873.title: Head and Neck Cancer Incidence, Mortality, and Disability-Adjusted Life Years From 1990 to 2021-A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study
pmc-12546873.creator: Yue Wang, Jingjing Zheng, Wenhao Ren, Shaoming Li, Keqian Zhi, Ling Gao
pmc-12546873.description: ObjectiveThis study evaluates the global burden of head and neck cancers, analyzing incidence, mortality, and DALYs from 1990 to 2021, across age groups and regions with varying SDI levels.Materials and MethodsData from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) database (1990-2021) was utilized to examine incidence, mortality, and DALYs for head and neck cancers.

pmc-12554416.title: Validation of the American Heart Association Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events Equations in Diverse Socioeconomic Groups: The All of Us Cohort
pmc-12554416.creator: Ashley Adanna Lewis, Adrian Matias Bacong, Latha Palaniappan, Tina Hernandez‐Boussard
pmc-12554416.description: BackgroundIn 2023, the American Heart Association PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equations were introduced as a tool to improve cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction. This study tests their performance in a diverse socioeconomic cohort.MethodsWe analyzed All of Us participants aged 30 to 79 years without baseline CVD who had required PREVENT input data over a 5.4‐year follow‐up.

pmc-13250221.title: Global, regional and national burden of maternal haemorrhage (2000–2021) and projections to 2050 in 204 countries and territories
pmc-13250221.creator: Mulat Ayele, Bereket Duko, Tenaw Tiruye, Paul R Ward, Lillian Mwanri, Gavin Pereira, Tegene Atamenta Kitaw, Biruk Beletew Abate, Eyob Shitie Lake, Abebaw Alamrew, Aynalem Yetwale, Gizachew Yilak, Befkad Derese Tilahun, Chalie Mulugeta, Tadele Emagneneh, Amanuel Tesfay Gebremedhin
pmc-13250221.description: ObjectiveTo estimate the global, regional and national burden of maternal haemorrhage (2000–2021) and its 2050 projections in 204 countries and territories.DesignThis study systematic analysis of the burden of maternal haemorrhage sourced data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study.

pmc-13374071.title: Intraoperative complications during gender-affirming laparoscopic hysterectomy in transgender men receiving testosterone: a case series
pmc-13374071.creator: Samaneh Rokhgireh, Sara Norouzi, Roya Derakhshan, Neda Hashemi, Maryam Pourbarghi, Zahra Salehi
pmc-13374071.description: BackgroundLaparoscopic hysterectomy is a core component of gender-affirming care for transgender men. However, long-term testosterone therapy can lead to anatomical and tissue changes that increase the complexity of pelvic surgery.ObjectiveTo describe the intraoperative complications encountered during gender-affirming laparoscopic hysterectomy in transgender men receiving testosterone therapy and discuss strategies for mitigation.

pmc-13430751.title: Modeling distress in cancer patients using a fuzzy logic approach based on expert consensus
pmc-13430751.creator: Anushk Pandey, Bejoy C Thomas, Manoj Pandey
pmc-13430751.description: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a fuzzy logic model based on expert consensus to elucidate distress dynamics in cancer patients, examining the non-linear interactions between psychological, social, and medical factors.MethodsA two-round Delphi process with 23 psychosocial oncology experts was conducted to generate an interaction matrix of 18 distress-related variables.

pmc-13514413.title: Coronary Artery Calcium Score and Carotid Intima-Media Thickness As Markers of Computed Tomography Angiographic Severity in Coronary Artery Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13514413.creator: Sachin Khanduri, Tariq Ahmad Imam, Sana, Shaista Ejaz, Deole Yash Milind, Sibtain Raza Khan, Nadeem Akhter, Rubina Saudi, Tanzeel Danish, Punyajeet Sardana

pmc-13632801.title: A Summer Educational Program for Early Medical Student Exposure to Multidisciplinary Oncology: A Pilot Experience
pmc-13632801.creator: Melinda Gevorgian, Leslie Harrell, Gary D Lewis, Santanu Samanta
pmc-13632801.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cancer remains the second leading cause of death in the United States, highlighting the need to strengthen the oncology workforce. Undergraduate medical education often lacks sufficient exposure to oncology, particularly radiation oncology, resulting in limited awareness of the specialty. Structured rotations in oncology, along with mentorship and research opportunities, have been shown to increase interest in oncology and support entry into these fields.
